$comment: The one home of villanelle's API concepts, members, kind lists, error groups, limits and reserved names (spec/spec.md is canonical for behaviour; this file is canonical for the lists). Names are spec names: lowercase words; a binding changes only the casing (spec/binding-guide.md rule 1) except where a member's 'spell' records an allowed difference. 'ts' and 'py' give each binding's spelling after milestone 1 (bead vil-fy4). Extracted from ts/ and py/ on feat/low-level-layer (PR 4) on 2026-10-28; 'disagreements' lists where they differed and what the spec picks.

naming.rule: The spec names each concept once in plain lowercase words; each binding only changes the casing.

ts.type: PascalCase; interfaces keep an I prefix until the owner answers binding-guide rule 2
ts.constant: PascalCase key of a constant object

py.kind value: StrEnum member UPPER_SNAKE_CASE whose value is the lowercase string

layers.name: shared
layers.holds: positions, places, origins, diagnostics, error groups, value kinds, expanded values and their readers

layers.name: io
layers.holds: the document source and writer ports, adapters, the extension port

layers.name: written
layers.holds: the low level: processor, document graph, documents, statements, values, variables

layers.name: rendered
layers.holds: the rendered tree: render (graph), directives, arguments, addresses, diff

layer direction: A layer imports only the layers in its 'may import' list. Nothing below the rendered layer imports, names or returns a rendered type (owner, 2026-10-29: "The low level shouldn't \"depend on\" the middle layer — they should have different domain objects. The middle layer of objects can build on the lower layer domains"). Going up a layer is the upper layer's free function: render (graph). Each binding enforces this with a check (frozen-m1.md).

token kind.values from: grammar/Villanelle.g4: its token names, in the order the grammar declares them (the grammar is their one home, so they are not copied here)

statement kind.ts: inline literal types on each statement interface
statement kind.py: Literal strings on each statement class

value kind.note: an expanded value's (and so a rendered argument's) kind is this list without 'reference'
value kind.ts: ValueKind (constant object; written values use inline literals and include 'reference', rendered ValueKind does not)
value kind.py: ValueKind (StrEnum, without 'reference'); written values use Literal strings

place kind.ts: inline literals on IPlace and IOverride
place kind.py: none: Place and Override are told apart by class (root cause 3)

unreadable reason.note: computed by the low level's binding (a statement copy it cannot expand) and shown by the rendered layer's unreadable; generated into the shared kinds module so neither layer imports the other for it

change kind.py: none: classes Added, Removed, Changed, Unknown without kind (root cause 3)

limits.name: nesting depth
limits.means: blocks and lists nested at most this deep

limits.name: expansion depth
limits.means: use and extension lines nested at most this deep

limits.name: integer range
limits.means: integer words and slice or index bounds lie within plus or minus this (2^53-1)

reserved names.also: the directive name of every registered extension

variable name.applies to: a $name without its $, an override name, a variable rename

program code.means: <namespace>/<name>, a program's own diagnostic code; villanelle's codes start with E

error groups.name: diagnostic error
error groups.raised when: a reader is given the wrong value, a program's error(...), or the root file cannot be read; carries one located diagnostic as 'diagnostic'

error groups.name: read error
error groups.raised when: load cannot resolve the root to exactly one file or read it (E3004 at the root path)

error groups.name: edit error
error groups.raised when: base of the errors an edit raises; nothing changed

error groups.name: bad text error
error groups.raised when: the text given to an edit, or an override's text, is not what it takes; 'diagnostics' are located in that text

error groups.name: detached error
error groups.raised when: any member but kind of a detached handle is used

error groups.name: no set line error
error groups.raised when: set or rename on a variable with no set line (a parameter or an override)

error groups.name: save error
error groups.raised when: the writer failed; 'files' is what was handed over, the cause is the writer's failure

error groups.name: argument type error
error groups.raised when: an argument of the wrong type, above all anything but text where villanelle text is taken (spec 6.9)
error groups.new in: milestone 1 (owner, 2026-10-29: 'A Keep text only, make misuse impossible')

error groups.name: misuse error
error groups.raised when: a bad argument value a program could have checked: a bad variable or override name, a program code without '/', a reserved or repeated extension name

error groups.name: index out of range
error groups.raised when: an insert index outside a block; a token range outside a parse

argument type error message.rule: One helper per binding builds it (one home); every member that takes villanelle text, quote, rename, set override and each load override call it before changing anything. Messages are for people (spec 2.3); the class and the member and parameter named are the contract.
argument type error message.ts: `${member}(): argument "${parameter}" must be a string, not ${got}; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, String() a number`
argument type error message.py: f"{member}() argument '{parameter}' must be str, not {type(value).__name__}; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, str() a number"
argument type error message.member: the member in the binding's casing, as the caller wrote it: set, replaceWithText / replace_with_text, insertStatements / insert_statements, addStatements / add_statements, setOverride / set_override, rename, quote, load
argument type error message.parameter: text; name for rename and for set override's name; overrides["<name>"] for a load override
argument type error message.example py: TypeError: set() argument 'text' must be str, not int; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, str() a number
argument type error message.example ts: TypeError: set(): argument "text" must be a string, not number; villanelle edits take text: quote() a program string, String() a number
